trust_decision.summary: A URL that will receive the agent's OAuth2 client_id/client_secret must be https, or http on a literal loopback host; the decision lives in utcp_http._security.ensure_secure_url, which at the pinned commit is applied to manual-discovery and tool-invocation URLs but never to OAuth2Auth.token_url, neither when an OpenAPI spec is converted nor when a protocol fetches the token.

landing_point.why: The summary names utcp-http's OpenAPI conversion; this is the only place where a remote spec's tokenUrl is turned into an OAuth2Auth.token_url, and it does so with no URL check (the identical Swagger 2.0 branch is at openapi_converter.py:386-398).

fix_sites.entry_point: OpenApiConverter.convert() (public converter API; also reached from FileCommunicationProtocol.register_manual at plugins/communication_protocols/file/src/utcp_file/file_communication_protocol.py:74 and TextCommunicationProtocol.register_manual at plugins/communication_protocols/text/src/utcp_text/text_communication_protocol.py:66), OpenAPI 3.0 flows branch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: utcp-gql ships no `utcp.plugins` entry point (compare plugins/communication_protocols/websocket/pyproject.toml:43-44), carries an empty `INCOMPLETE` marker at plugins/communication_protocols/gql/INCOMPLETE, and is absent from the CI install/test lists, so a solver can call the GraphQL plugin unfinished and outside a utcp-http advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: token_url may legitimately be an injected variable such as "${TOKEN_URL}": the project recommends injected variables for this field and substitutes them only later, at register/call time, so a check placed at config-load/serializer time or inside the converter rejects the unsubstituted placeholder and breaks a documented legitimate configuration. The converter also has an established explicit-exception precedent for base_url overrides that a careless fix would not mirror.

O6_input_shapes: plain-http literal-loopback token URL such as http://127.0.0.1:PORT/token (accepted; existing OAuth2 tests use exactly this shape, e.g. plugins/communication_protocols/http/tests/test_http_communication_protocol.py:198)
plain-http internal/metadata token URL such as http://169.254.169.254/token (must be rejected)
hostname-prefix look-alikes http://localhost.evil.com and http://127.0.0.1.attacker.example (must be rejected as non-loopback)
token_url supplied directly on an OAuth2Auth in a call template or client config, with no OpenAPI conversion involved
both credential placements at the token POST: form body vs HTTP Basic auth header

O8b_injection_room.sibling: OAuth2 token fetch in the MCP plugin (same POST of client_id/client_secret to auth_details.token_url, no URL check, no redirect re-validation)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The plugin already contains a verbatim copy of the http/SSE `_handle_oauth2` implementation and its call template declares `auth: Optional[OAuth2Auth]` (plugins/communication_protocols/mcp/src/utcp_mcp/mcp_call_template.py:133) with a documented OAuth2 example, so wiring that field up is the obvious next maintainer step and would inherit the same open sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: pydantic field validator on OAuth2Auth.token_url instead of per-protocol checks at the sink
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Auth models are shared by every protocol and round-trip through OAuth2AuthSerializer, so centralising the check here is the natural DRY fix a maintainer would reach for; it is also the trap, because config-load validation runs before DefaultVariableSubstitutor (utcp_client_implementation.py:123,370) resolves ${...} placeholders.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second spec source (OpenAPI document carried in text content) that produces tools with OAuth2 auth via OpenApiConverter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This plugin and the file plugin already reuse OpenApiConverter, so adding another converter front-end is a realistic maintainer change; a solver who patches only the converter call path used in the report would still cover it, but a solver who patches only the http registration path would not.

O9_family: server-side request forgery / trust-boundary bypass with credential exfiltration (CWE-918)

O10_build.toolchain: pip + setuptools, one editable install per package (core, plugins/communication_protocols/*), pytest + pytest-asyncio (+ pytest-aiohttp for the http plugin)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate tokenUrl only inside OpenApiConverter._extract_auth, the report's landing point: that rejects ${VAR}-templated token URLs that are substituted only later and leaves a token_url supplied directly in a call template or client config unguarded at every protocol's _handle_oauth2.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit also carries GHSA-9qhg-99ww-9mqc (redirect-following SSRF on every aiohttp request) and GHSA-ppx3-28rw-8fpf (startswith hostname-prefix bypass in the gql and websocket plugins); noted once, not assessed here.
